decision_reason: A1 already provides an adequate gravity-relative posture hierarchy for lying down, but running has the weakest seen-prototype coverage and forms a close unseen pair with jogging. Their A1 distinction relies mainly on cadence, smoothness and impulsiveness, so vertical whole-body motion is added as an independent locomotor contrast. Translation-direction reversal is added to distinguish progressive running from the nearby seen anchor jump front & back. The broad rotational_motion concept is split by body region to separate waist bends forward from knees bending (crouching) and frontal elevation of arms using the available chest, lower-arm and ankle sensing. motion_regularity is dropped because every supplied class prototype has the same level and therefore it contributes no split-specific semantic contrast.

attributes.name: motion_intensity
attributes.definition: Overall magnitude and energy of motion within a window, including both linear and rotational components.

attributes.name: cadence
attributes.definition: Rate at which a meaningful periodic motion unit repeats over time. Cadence measures repetitions per unit time, not the total number of repetitions in the recording.

levels.Low: No clear periodic repetition or a slow repetition rate.

attributes.name: smoothness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion changes continuously rather than through sustained rapid fluctuations.

levels.Medium: Moderately smooth motion with some fluctuations.
levels.High: Continuous and smooth motion with little fluctuation.

attributes.name: impulsiveness
attributes.definition: Degree to which motion contains short, abrupt, high-magnitude changes or impacts.

levels.Low: Few or no pronounced abrupt peaks.

attributes.name: posture_inclination
attributes.definition: Average gravity-relative inclination of the global load-bearing body configuration within a window, rather than the orientation of an isolated moving limb.

levels.High: Strongly inclined or nearly horizontal relative to gravity.

attributes.name: posture_variability
attributes.definition: Extent to which the global load-bearing body configuration changes relative to gravity within a window, rather than local limb-orientation changes.

attributes.name: trunk_angular_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular change in the chest or trunk configuration during the activity, excluding angular motion confined mainly to distal limbs.

levels.Low: Little or no trunk angular motion.

attributes.name: distal_limb_angular_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of angular motion expressed at the instrumented right lower arm or left ankle, rather than through global trunk reorientation.

levels.Low: Little or no distal-limb angular motion.

attributes.name: translational_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of sustained linear progression or locomotor translation within a window.

levels.High: Prominent sustained translational or locomotor motion.

attributes.name: vertical_motion
attributes.definition: Prominence of repeated whole-body translational motion along the gravity axis, distinct from changes caused only by body inclination.

levels.Low: Little or no repeated vertical whole-body motion.

attributes.name: translation_direction_reversal
attributes.definition: Degree to which translational motion repeatedly reverses direction within a window rather than maintaining one main direction of progression.

levels.Low: No sustained translation or predominantly one-directional translation.

operations.reason: Overall motion energy remains a transferable distinction between static postures, moderate activities and vigorous locomotion.
Repetition rate is directly supported by periodicity and provides an important ordered contrast between jogging and running, with walking and cycling supplying seen locomotor anchors.
Sustained rapid signal fluctuation distinguishes smoother bending and cycling patterns from more abrupt running and jumping patterns independently of average energy.
Peak impacts provide a physically supported contrast between vigorous foot-strike activities and smooth posture-changing activities.
Gravity-relative mean posture already gives a direct transferable hierarchy from standing through sitting to lying and supports lying down without inventing a new posture label.
Gravity-angle variation separates sustained postures from repeated global configuration changes and transfers from knees bending (crouching) to waist bends forward.

A single rotational degree conflates trunk flexion, arm elevation and ankle-driven cyclic motion. Chest acceleration can support trunk orientation change, while lower-arm and ankle gyroscopes support distal-limb angular motion. The split adds a transferable body-region contrast for waist bends forward against the seen crouching and arm-elevation anchors.
Sustained progression remains the primary transferable distinction between locomotor activities and in-place posture or limb movements.
The supplied A1 prototypes assign High motion_regularity to every seen and unseen class, so the concept contributes no split-specific separation despite being observable in principle.

Gravity-referenced acceleration and translational proxies can represent vertical whole-body motion. This adds an independent intensity-related contrast for the close jogging-running pair and transfers through walking, climbing stairs and jump front & back.

Short-window velocity proxies and multiaxial motion structure can distinguish repeated front-back reversal from sustained progression. This prevents the nearest seen anchor jump front & back from being semantically confounded with running solely because both are vigorous and impact-rich.

semantic_redundancy_review: The final dimensions are related but not duplicates. motion_intensity measures overall energy; vertical_motion isolates its gravity-axis translational component; impulsiveness measures short peaks; and smoothness measures sustained rapid fluctuation. cadence measures repetition rate rather than predictability, allowing the nondiscriminative motion_regularity dimension to be removed. posture_inclination measures mean global posture, posture_variability measures its temporal range, and trunk_angular_motion measures dynamic trunk rotation. distal_limb_angular_motion is body-region-specific and therefore distinct from trunk motion. translational_motion measures the prominence of sustained progression, whereas translation_direction_reversal describes whether that progression repeatedly changes direction. All retained or introduced attributes are ordinal and are supported in principle by gravity orientation, gyroscopic rotation, motion energy, periodicity, jerk, gravity-angle variation, translational proxies or multiaxial coupling.

_meta.validation: Semantic schema and complete A1-to-A2 lineage validated; no feature binding performed.
